name: Welding cell
summary: Four KUKA KR 210 robots weld a car body frame on a sled: a laser seam camera with a learned network finds the car (±3 cm) and tracks every seam; learn on the GPU (or the CPU), then run the line car af
help: What to do: Learn to follow the seams trains the seam camera's network on simulated laser profiles (on an NVIDIA GPU when the machine has one, otherwise on the CPU, with Accelerator auto) and, every couple of minutes, welds a whole car with it; the network goes out as seam_tracker_<date>_<p95>um.pt (send it to a dataset wired back to Seam tracker so learning goes on from it). Run the production line (any machine) welds car after car with the newest network: the sled brings the car in (it stops within ±3 cm), the four robots read two reference points each with their laser line and find the car's position and turn, then weld their seams following the camera, and the car leaves for the next one. Seam camera off (or no network yet) welds the taught programme as it is, to compare. Each robot works out by itself which way round to weld each seam, how to lean the torch and from which arm pose. 3D, live: wire this block's telemetry and the Welding robot model block's output to a 3D view (and that output also to Robot model here, so this block starts after it): one robot (3D view: robot shown live) moves with its joints while the cars are welded, with the rails, the sled, the car's floor and the car's seams (blue to weld, orange welded). 3D, replay: wire the welding-cell-models dataset (kr210_weld.glb, s15_frame.glb) to Models and the 3D scene output to another 3D view: when the block has finished, the newest five cars replay there with all four robots, the seams in yellow on the frame and a blue dot at each wire tip while it welds. Results: every weld (worst and mean distance from the real seam, in mm) and every car (where it really was and where the robots found it, cycle time).

inputs.label: Seam tracker
inputs.help: The weld-tracker dataset (seam_tracker_*.pt): the line uses the newest; learning goes on from it

inputs.label: Models
inputs.help: The welding-cell-models dataset: kr210_weld.glb (the robot with its torch) and s15_frame.glb (the car frame). Without them, boxes stand in in the 3D view

inputs.label: Robot model
inputs.help: The Welding robot model block's output: the block starts after it, so the robot is already in the 3D view when the first car comes in

outputs.label: Seam tracker
outputs.help: Learn: seam_tracker_<date>_<p95>um.pt (the network and its scores)

outputs.label: Welds
outputs.help: Line: welds.csv, one row per seam of every car

outputs.label: Cars
outputs.help: Line: cars.csv, where each car really was and where the robots found it, cycle time, worst weld

outputs.label: 3D scene
outputs.help: welding_cell.scene.json (esasim.scene/1: the newest five cars, every robot part posed) and the robot parts and car frame as GLB: wire it to a 3D view

params.label: Accelerator
params.help: auto: an NVIDIA GPU when the machine has one, otherwise the CPU (learning is several times slower there). The production line needs no GPU

params.label: 3D view: robot shown live
params.help: The robot whose joints go live to EsaSim's 3D view (the same as in the Welding robot model block)

params.label: Weld tolerance (mm)
params.help: A seam passes when the wire never strays further than this from the real seam

params.label: Car turned on the sled (± deg)
Frame build variation (mm)
params.help: How far each car's seams wander from the drawing

params.label: Seam camera
params.help: Off: weld the taught programme as it is, to compare
